title: Bridge review queue: clarify PRD dependency checkpoints and acceptance pipeline
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Background: Multiple recent PRDs (privacy-sensitive prompt-sets, private deployment upgrade, and KV cache telemetry) have stalled during interlock because reviewers lack a consistent checkpoints list. Objective: Create a lightweight 'bridge review queue' pattern and a short artifact checklist so Engineering, Design and Legal can clear dependencies with predictable SLAs. Scope: define the queue, checklist artifacts, fast-track lanes for low-risk changes, escalation owner, and automated reminders. Out-of-scope: deep technical design for runtime internals (handled by ENG tickets) and legal contract negotiations. Constraints: limited legal bandwidth (peak weeks), design sprint ending 2026-03-18, and two-week feature freeze for Dedicated capacity starting 2026-03-20. Success metrics: decrease PRD review cycle time from median 14 days to <=6 days for cross-team reviews; reduce ad hoc blocking comments by 60%.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A published Bridge Review Queue runbook exists in Confluence with a 6-item artifact checklist (PRD link, acceptance criteria, test plan, data residency map, proposed UI screenshots, rollback plan)
A2: Legal, Design, and Eng owners listed for each PRD type and assigned an SLA (48h for minor, 72h for major) in the runbook
A3: Two pilot PRDs (PRD-A: privacy-prompt-sets, PRD-B: private-upgrade-lite) complete the full queue cycle with no unresolved dependency older than 72 hours
A4: Automated Slack reminders integrated with the queue (reminder cadence documented) and at least one case of fast-track approval exercised
A5: A follow-up retrospective note in Confluence with measured review cycle-times and feedback logged
comments: 2026-03-10 Marco Alvarez: Created ticket after blocked PRD review for privacy prompt-sets. Initial ask: define a repeatable review pattern and checklist. Tagged Legal and Design owners.

2026-03-11 Priya Nandakumar: Drafted artifact checklist and proposed SLAs. Pushed Confluence stub: see links. Asked Legal to confirm whether 'data residency map' is sufficient or if contract-level review needed.

2026-03-12 Aisha Kapoor (Legal): Legal redlines to checklist: require explicit data flow diagram for any telemetry changes and an opt-in text sample for consent flows; timeline noted (may take up to 4 business days for major contract changes).
2026-03-13 Daniel Park (Design): Shared updated consent modal variants in Figma and proposed smaller A/B matrix to reduce review surface; recommends fast-track for UI copy-only changes.

2026-03-14 Ravi Shah (Eng): Flagged dependency ENG-42107 (KV cache telemetry gating) — engineering indicates gated schema migration that needs a separate rollout plan. Proposed splitting PRD into 'front-end acceptance' and 'runtime migration' slices.

2026-03-15 Priya Nandakumar: Scope decision: adopt slice approach. Action items assigned: (1) Marco to finalize runbook checklist, (2) Aisha to confirm SLA exceptions for contract-level items, (3) Daniel to mark UI-only assets for fast-track. Set first pilot kickoff 2026-03-16.
notes: Trade-offs considered: enforcing a long checklist increases upfront friction but reduces late discovery; decided to keep checklist minimal and add optional deep-dive attachments.
Fallback plan: if Legal cannot meet SLA for a major item, route to 'escalation owner' (Head of Legal) and create a temporary acceptance token that limits feature to internal beta.
Follow-ups: log measurable before/after metrics and consider automating 'queue heartbeat' in the Console to surface PRDs awaiting cross-team signoff.
